candidates.rationale: Reproduced independently from primary sources (adr-base-4015c15.md, adr-head-83a22d8.md, and the unified diff). Base C63 at line 3328 reads verbatim 'R08: retention release is the eleventh effect action and requires a complete root-set epoch CAS/reachability proof.' (lane cited ~3325; off by 3 lines, immaterial, text matches exactly). The base effect-action matrix (text at base line 2615, 'from these eleven rows') has exactly 11 table rows; HEAD's matrix (head line 2945, text 'from these twelve rows') has exactly 12 rows, the added row being retention_root_admission (head line 2960). HEAD's C63 (head line 3741) was generalized to 'retention release is an authorized effect action...', dropping the ordinal claim rather than updating it to reflect the new row or adding a companion finding. I read all 95 checklist items C01-C95 in HEAD (lines 3679-3773) in full; none references retention_root_admission by name or by an unambiguous paraphrase -- the only other 'retention' hits are C29 (general retention-roots lineage, unrelated to admission-specific mechanics) and C63 itself. The control is fully specified elsewhere: section 12.3 'Discriminated Authorization Subjects' defines retention_root_admission_target (head line 2940) and the matrix row (head line 2960); section 12.4 'One-Way Anti-Replay' contains a full prose paragraph (head lines 3022-3033) describing admission as 'atomic and symmetric to release', its CAS mechanics, and its result/proof artifacts; section 12.7 'Schema-Specific Verification Profiles' lists retention_root_admission_result/v1 and retention_root_admission_proof/v1 at head lines 3612-3613, matching the lane's cited range exactly. I additionally verified there is no 1:1 coverage promise anywhere in the document: a full-text search for 'checklist', 'one-to-one'/'1:1', and phrases like 'each row has a checklist item' found zero matches tying the matrix to the C01-C95 table; the C01-C95 table's own section header is '13.1 Gate 2 Remediation Closure Map' with columns 'Finding'|'Normative closure' -- it is framed as a closure map for specific Gate-2 findings, not a declared mirror of the effect-action matrix's row count. This means the gap is completeness, not an internal contradiction. As additional corroborating context (not part of the lane's original claim): C46, the checklist item that DOES describe the matrix as a whole, was also edited in this diff (base line 3311 'closed eleven-row role/action/side/subject/predecessor/result/slot matrix' -> head line 3724 'closed role/action/side/subject/predecessor/result/slot matrix', i.e. the row-count qualifier was dropped entirely rather than updated to 'twelve-row'). This shows the same edit pattern (generalize away the stale count) was applied consistently at both C46 and C63, which is more consistent with a deliberate/systematic drafting choice than an isolated oversight, though it still leaves no C-item that names the new action explicitly. Net: the lane's factual claims are all confirmed as stated (matrix 11->12 rows, C63 generalized, 0 C-items name the new action, control fully specified in 12.3/12.4 prose and 12.7 schema table, no 1:1 promise exists). This is a real, verifiable completeness gap in a documentation closure-map artifact for a governance ADR, not a regression in the underlying control, which is fully specified and traceable through the ADR's other normative sections.

summary: sdf-003 is CONFIRMED as a real, Low-severity, non-blocking completeness gap. Independent reproduction from primary sources matches every factual element of the lane's claim: base C63 text and line, matrix growing from 11 to 12 rows with the new retention_root_admission row, C63's generalization in HEAD, zero references to retention_root_admission across all 95 checklist items (C01-C95, all read in full), and full specification of the control in ADR prose sections 12.3-12.4 plus the schema-profile table at 12.7 (lines 3612-3613, exactly as the lane cited). No 1:1 coverage promise between the effect-action matrix and the C01-C95 closure-map table exists anywhere in the document (that table is explicitly scoped as a 'Gate 2 Remediation Closure Map' for findings, not a matrix mirror), so this is documentation-index incompleteness rather than an internal contradiction or a regression in the underlying governance control. Not blocking for merge of a governance-documentation PR; recommend a fast-follow to add or extend a C-item referencing retention_root_admission (and to decide whether C46 should be restored to state 'twelve-row' or intentionally stay unquantified) for closure-map completeness.
